points.quote: `workbench.desktop.main.ts` and `workbench.web.main.ts` each start with `import './workbench.common.main.js'`. They then add their own platform-specific imports and service registrations.

They then add their own platform-specific imports and service registrations. The web file, for example, adds `contrib/webview/browser/webview.web.contribution.js` and `contrib/extensions/browser/extensions.web.contribution.js`.
`src/vs/workbench/workbench.common.main.ts` is the shared entry point. ... `workbench.desktop.main.ts` and `workbench.web.main.ts` each start with `import './workbench.common.main.js'`.
A `browser` module cannot import `node` or `electron-browser` code, so a shared feature can only reach platform-specific behaviour through a service interface that each platform implements.
The source-organization doc says that "Only code referenced from entry point files is loaded."
A feature's `*.contribution.ts` file registers its services, commands, views and so on when it is imported.
